_comment: Static onboarding curation, keyed by paper. Authored once — NOT generated per visit. A brand-new visitor is shown a single, minimal landing that opens the "featured" paper (its pre-placed annotations demo every feature). Snippets are VERBATIM substrings of the rendered article so the in-page locator can place highlights. URLs are web-rendered (distill.pub / ar5iv.org) where DOM locating is reliable; arXiv /abs/ links render as PDF and won't auto-place. Each item may set "feature": discuss|citation|math|code — clicking the highlight auto-runs that feature. math/code items carry a "tex" string (used directly, no MathML extraction); citation items carry a "cite" marker (e.g. "[13]") that drives the matcher while "snippet" just anchors the highlight. "featured" selects which paper the landing opens; "startLabel" sets the landing button text. Extra papers can stay here for later reuse even if not currently featured.

zoom-in-circuits.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
zoom-in-circuits.hook: What if individual neurons — and the connections between them — are legible algorithms?

items.snippet: rich inner world within our models
items.note: The motivation for the whole program: weights aren't a black box — there's a legible inner world to map.

items.snippet: What if we treated individual neurons, even individual weights, as being worthy of serious investigation?
items.note: The mindset shift that kicked off mechanistic interpretability — zoom in instead of explaining the whole net at once.

items.snippet: You can watch a circle detector be assembled from curves.
items.note: A concrete 'circuit': simple features composing into a more complex one, like parts on an assembly line.

attention-is-all-you-need.title: Attention Is All You Need
attention-is-all-you-need.hook: The 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer and reshaped modern AI.

items.snippet: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
items.note: The core bet: drop RNNs and convolutions entirely, lean on attention alone. Click to ask Claude why that was radical in 2017.

items.snippet: Recurrent neural networks, long short-term memory
items.note: There's a citation right here. Click to watch Claude pull up the cited paper and explain why it's relevant.

items.snippet: We compute the matrix of outputs as
items.note: Scaled dot-product attention. Click 'Explain math' to have Claude unpack it term by term.

items.snippet: In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously
items.note: Same equation — click 'To code' to get a runnable PyTorch/NumPy version with tensor shapes.

most-research-false.title: Why Most Published Research Findings Are False
most-research-false.hook: A statistician's provocative argument that most published findings don't hold up.

items.snippet: It can be proven that most claimed research findings are false
items.note: The provocative thesis in one line. Click to discuss how Ioannidis actually argues it.

items.snippet: the post-study probability that it is true is the positive predictive value
items.note: The formula behind the claim. Click 'Explain math' to see what power, bias, and prior odds each do.

feature-visualization.title: Feature Visualization
feature-visualization.hook: Hallucinate the images that make each neuron fire — and see what the network is really looking for.

items.snippet: Starting from random noise, we optimize an image to activate a particular neuron
items.note: The trick in one sentence: optimize the image, not the weights, to reveal what a neuron loves.

items.snippet: We find that remarkably simple methods can produce high-quality visualizations.
items.note: Reassuring result — you don't need heavy machinery to peek inside a vision model.
